data.title: Soros Fund ramps up Intel stake to over $340 million in third quarter
data.description: Nov 13 : Soros Fund Management, the family office of billionaire George Soros, significantly raised its stake in Intel in the third quarter, a regulatory filing showed on Friday. Here are more details: • The investment firm built a 2.83 million-share position valued at $340.3 million as it boosted its exposure to the major PC chip supplier • The fund had held just 100,000 Intel shares at the end of June, according to its previous quarterly disclosure, marking one of the most striking changes in its portfolio • Intel's stock took a hammering late last month after the chipmaker warned of a severe cash burn this year due to the faltering PC market, bottlenecks in manufacturing ‌and heavy spending on expanding production • Still, the stock is up nearly 62 per cent year to date, as the company benefits from surging demand for AI data-center CPUs • The fund cut its stake in Apple by 25.7 per cent to 393,680 shares and in ON Semiconductor by 92.7 per cent to 16,594 shares • The disclosures on Friday were made through the so-called 13F regulatory filings, which show investment firms' portfolios and are closely watched for trends even though the data is released with a delay

data.title: US National Weather Service reports nationwide internet, communications issues
data.description: Nov 13 : The US National Weather Service said on Friday it was experiencing nationwide internet and communications problems that could prevent users from accessing products on its websites or cause outdated information to be displayed. Technicians were working to resolve the problems as soon as possible, the NWS said in a statement.

data.title: Exclusive-Investors flock to Anthropic IPO but question durability of AI lead
data.description: Nov 13 : Institutional-investor interest in Anthropic’s initial public offering is outpacing the early days of SpaceX's roadshow, according to two people familiar with the companies’ offerings. The Anthropic roadshow is scheduled to run through next Wednesday, when the AI company is expected to price the $64 billion deal. Anthropic and its investment banks are meeting prospective investors in New York, Boston and San Francisco to gauge demand for the offering, one of the people and a third person familiar with the matter said.  The IPO drew about two times the orders for the shares available by the end of Tuesday, the first day of the roadshow, one of the people said. By the end of Thursday, the book was six times oversubscribed, one other person said. SpaceX’s IPO was two times oversubscribed by the end of its second day of roadshow, Reuters previously reported. While that single-digit subscription rate would be considered modest for many highly anticipated IPOs, bankers and investors said demand is impressive for the Anthropic offering given the size of the IPO. They expect Anthropic's order book to grow substantially as the roadshow progresses, reflecting strong early demand, two of the people said. Details of the IPO, including the demand for shares, could change, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity. Anthropic declined to comment. During the roadshow, investors are grappling with two fundamental questions as they assess the offering and the company's valuation: whether Anthropic can maintain its lead as competitors such as Alphabet’s Google rapidly catch up in developing advanced AI models, and whether its Claude chatbot can maintain its lead beyond coding, in the broader market for knowledge workers. TIME OF UNCERTAINTY IN AI The questions underscore the challenge of valuing a company whose revenue is growing fast but whose long-term competitive position remains uncertain. Investors are trying to determine whether the AI industry will ultimately be dominated by one or two players or support several leading companies, and whether Anthropic can sustain premium pricing if rivals offer comparable models. Meanwhile, investors are also weighing the limitations of the information Anthropic is providing during its IPO roadshow. One investor who attended a roadshow meeting said the company had not provided detailed answers to some of the questions raised. Anthropic declined to comment on the investor's remarks. While companies are not always able to address every investor question during roadshows, some investors remain cautious about an offering at a high valuation amid a broader shakeout in the AI sector, with the limited disclosure leaving some questions unanswered. One of the group meetings during the roadshow also did not include a conference call allowing institutional investors to dial in and ask questions, according to an investor who attended that meeting — a departure from standard roadshow practice. Representatives from Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley largely read from prepared remarks rather than solicit  questions at that meeting, the person added. Morgan Stanley declined to comment. Goldman Sachs did not immediately respond to a request for comment. REVENUE AT CENTER OF VALUATION DEBATE Investors are arriving at widely different estimates of how quickly Anthropic's revenue will grow, creating a broad range of potential valuation outcomes. The key figure underpinning valuation models is Anthropic's projected 2028 revenue, which banks estimate at around $270 billion to $280 billion and use to apply enterprise-value-to-revenue multiples and arrive at their valuation estimates, two of the people familiar with the projections said. For a high-growth company like Anthropic, investors typically give significant weight to future revenue growth when assessing its value. Some sell-side projections put Anthropic's revenue at around $52 billion to $53 billion in 2026, rising to $135 billion to $137 billion in  2027, one of the people said. Certain buy-side projections are running 10 per cent to 15 per cent higher for 2026 and 2027, an investor who has placed an order in the IPO said. But buy-side forecasts also vary significantly. One investor who conducted due diligence on the IPO but decided not to participate has a more conservative outlook that is about 30 per cent below the sell-side estimate for 2028. Differences between sell-side and buy-side forecasts are common. Sell-side analysts' estimates tend to track a company's own projections more closely, while investors may build in more optimistic or conservative assumptions about future growth. Companies, in turn, have an incentive to set conservative targets ahead of an IPO, leaving room to beat estimates and raise expectations after listing. The comparable companies used in the valuation models also reflect the difficulty of finding direct peers for Anthropic. SpaceX and cybersecurity company CrowdStrike are among the names being used as benchmarks, one of the people familiar with the projections said. The focus on Anthropic's projected 2028 revenue contrasts with SpaceX, whose valuation case relied on projected 2029 revenue that some investors viewed as particularly aggressive. Anthropic's valuation debate, by comparison, is anchored in a forecast for a year closer to its expected public listing.  ​

data.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet, letting AI agents pay for purchases
data.description: Nov 13 : OpenAI said on Friday it has launched ChatGPT Wallet, which lets AI agents pay for purchases without accessing users' card details, with a security check required for every transaction. Here are more details: • The wallet has been built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, OpenAI said • It will initially be available in the US to ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and older with eligible US-issued cards. It can be accessed through "dots", the company's always-on AI agents • Users can review items, the total and the selected card before each purchase, then approve it with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan • The payment network will provide a payment token in place of the actual card details, so neither the business nor the agent can see them, the company said • OpenAI expects users to eventually delegate purchases to agents within certain set parameters, such as spending limits, categories or time periods

data.title: Commentary: Jensen Huang may prove that the ‘irreplaceable CEO’ is a myth
data.description: NEW YORK: “He’s irreplaceable,” Larry Ellison said. The year was 2009 and Oracle’s then-chief executive officer was talking about his friend Steve Jobs, who had recently returned to lead Apple after a liver transplant. Pundits would later go on to say the same about Jeff Bezos, that Amazon.com’s founder and CEO had “no viable successor”. (Both companies, of course, would go on to do just fine without their founders.) It’s worth remembering those prophecies as that word - irreplaceable - gets bandied around with abandon about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down Thursday (Nov 12) after nearly a week of turmoil at the company he cofounded and the industry he anchored.  One of many examples: “I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership,” Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire posted on X, a sentiment Elon Musk endorsed. Revelations from the New York Times on Wednesday, that Huang had an extramarital relationship with the company’s vice president of healthcare, made it impossible for the board to let him keep his job. While less shocking than Huang’s earlier admission that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, he had clearly violated the company’s code of conduct to “avoid situations where our actions create a conflict”. Before board members could make the case that Huang was the victim of a honeypot scheme. But there’s no convenient explanation for a relationship with a subordinate.CAN NVIDIA SURVIVE WITHOUT JENSEN HUANG? The board named CFO Collette Kress as the interim CEO, but now its members will have to plan for a future without Huang at the helm. This appears to be something they had rarely considered before, after allowing Huang to structure the company almost entirely around himself. The question now is whether he had also built it to survive without him. As Harvard Business School professor Rakesh Khurana put it to me: “The difference between a cult and a religion is that one outlasts the other.” At Nvidia, the evidence suggests that Huang created a system much more akin to the former.  The company has no chairman, no number two and no public succession plan. Huang had 60 direct reports whose job it was to quickly carry out his decisions, Bloomberg News has reported. Few other executives had a broad purview or responsibilities and instead focused on narrow products or technologies. Other executives had some public exposure but were always overshadowed by Huang, who delivered hours-long keynotes at events.  On earnings calls, as the Wall Street Journal noted, Huang fielded questions from analysts mostly by himself, leaving scripted comments to others - a regular practice at Nvidia but atypical at other companies. His board lacked the expected heavy hitters for a company of its size and import; other than Huang, it has no sitting CEOs.A REAL FAILURE OF LEADERSHIP? None of that necessarily means Huang can’t be replaced. There was no finding another Jobs or Bezos either - they were both singular leaders. But what they did, which appears to be missing at Nvidia, was methodically build companies designed to carry on their doctrines without them. Both created internal structures that institutionalised their ways of operating and thinking that allowed their successors to thrive: Apple’s stock returned nearly 2,800 per cent during Tim Cook’s 15-year tenure as CEO that ended in September; Andy Jassy has overseen a roughly 50 per cent increase since he took over at Amazon in 2021. At Apple, Jobs was a micromanager who was involved in every detail of the company. But he also taught employees to anticipate how he would solve problems. “The organization has been thoroughly trained to think like Steve,” Fortune reported in 2009. “People could envision, ‘This is what Steve would do.'”  He also had a clear number two in Cook, a manufacturing and supply chain guru, who had a trial run as CEO when Jobs was out on medical leave. Jobs made sure it wasn’t always the Steve Jobs show either. Cook and other executives were given public exposure by appearing alongside him on stage and on earnings calls. (It’s worth noting that Cook is being floated as a possible replacement for Huang, including by President Trump.) At Amazon, Bezos turned his management philosophy into an actionable way of operating - a set of leadership principles that Jassy and other executives helped him write. Bezos picked Jassy as his first shadow, a role in which he followed around the CEO for about 18 months. That’s when the two came up with the idea for Amazon Web Services, and then Bezos gave Jassy a wide berth to run it. By the time Jassy was tapped as CEO, he had already run a hugely important and valuable business. Part of the genius of both Bezos and Jobs was that they figured out how to turn their personal capabilities into corporate culture and competencies.  The parallels are hard to find at Nvidia, which is a real failure of leadership by Huang. His successor will have to figure out how to run a company built around someone who is no longer there. That should be one part of Huang’s legacy that no one tries to replicate.

data.title: AI rockets to top of worries about financial system in latest Fed survey
data.description: WASHINGTON, Nov 13 : Risks tied to the artificial intelligence sector surged to become the top-cited concern for financial stability, according to a semi-annual report released by the Federal Reserve on Friday. The US central bank's Financial Stability Report found potential risks from the technology itself and the breakneck investment in the sector as the preeminent concern of survey respondents. Eighty-seven percent of contacts surveyed cited AI as a salient risk to the financial system, as respondents pointed to worries about cyberattacks, risks associated with complex forms of AI-related financing, and the possibility of an AI earnings slowdown spurring a broad market correction. Just 50 per cent of those surveyed cited AI as a risk in the May version of the Fed's survey. Other top concerns cited in the survey also had heavy AI implications. The second most-cited concern was regarding a broad correction in risk assets at 52 per cent of those surveyed, and cyberattacks specifically were flagged as a worry by 43 per cent of respondents. Forty-eight percent of those surveyed also fretted about higher long-term interest rates, while 43 per cent cited fiscal debt sustainability as a worry. The survey was conducted in September and October, meaning respondents weighed in before the latest turmoil at chipmaker Nvidia, where CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving Chinese businesswoman whom the New York Times has reported is under suspicion as a Chinese spy. The survey also preceded the results of recent midterm elections in which the American public's rising concerns about AI were also a central issue. The increased focus on AI was underpinned by the report itself, as the Fed devoted a chunk of the report to examining the rapid increase in debt issuance tied to data centers and other advanced computing infrastructure. The Fed report found that advanced computing-related debt issuance had surged to $680 billion by October 2026, already a fivefold increase on debt issued in all of 2023. Advanced computing-related borrowing now accounts for nearly a third of all nonfinancial investment-grade corporate debt issuance, after amounting to less than 6 per cent three years ago. The Fed noted in its report that the rapid influx of debt issuance and investment in AI-related infrastructure could be compared to the broadband telecom investment cycle of the late 1990s, although the Fed said it is possible the current investment cycle may soon surpass that era. And the central bank focused on the complex financing arrangements underpinning some of this investment, noting that arrangements like long-term contracts, leases and guarantees allow hyperscalers and other large firms to support financing such projects by smaller third parties, and graphics card designers and hyperscalers often further contribute to investments via equity. Data collected by the Fed found that debt, guarantees, and not-yet-commenced leases on this infrastructure could exceed $3 trillion. The Fed said such "circular financing" dynamics could allow the largest firms to absorb losses in the event of a downturn, minimizing the impact on the broader financial system. However, it could also mean that those firms' exposure to such a downturn could be "substantially larger" than indicated by their on-balance-sheet liabilities. "The complex interlinkages among firms engaged in the data center buildout, public credit markets, private lenders, and special purpose financing vehicles create vulnerabilities that necessitate close monitoring," the report stated. Elsewhere in the financial system, the Fed found that asset valuations across a range of classes remained high, due in part to investor enthusiasm about AI. The report noted that investment in the AI sector has been a significant driver of US economic growth this year, and an unexpected downturn in corporate earnings could prompt a market decline, tighter credit, and reduced investment, which would all weigh on the economy. Such a downturn could also be exacerbated by relatively high levels of leverage in some portions of the financial sector. The Fed noted in its level that leverage among hedge funds, particularly the largest firms, remains at the highest levels recorded since they began gathering such data in 2013.

data.title: Meta employees test prediction-market app, WSJ reports
data.description: Nov 13 : Meta Platforms' employees have begun testing a prediction-market app called Takes, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. Here are some details:  • Employees can wager on the outcome of questions or events using "cred," short for credibility, rather than real money, the report said • The app is not available to the public and it is unclear when, if ever, it will be released, according to the report • Meta did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment • Prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket are drawing Gen Z users, with just over 60 per cent of their users under the age of 35 years, according to a recent S&P Global Market Intelligence Kagan survey

data.title: Tabletop games' popularity holds up as people seek off-screen connections, Asmodee CEO says
data.description: (Specifies wording in paragraph 2 to clarify Asmodee publishes and distributes board games.) By Vera Dvorakova Nov 13 : Demand for tabletop games is holding strong as people seek ways to play together in person, Asmodee CEO Thomas Koegler told Reuters ahead of the busy end-of-year shopping season. Sweden-based Asmodee publishes and distributes many globally known board games such as Catan, Ticket to Ride and Carcassonne. It also distributes trading card games from other publishers, including Pokémon, Hasbro's Magic: The Gathering and Bandai Namco's One Piece trading card games. "What's clear is that our industry benefits from very strong sociological dynamics of spending time with your loved ones," Koegler said in an interview on Friday. He expects game nights to remain a popular Saturday plan, especially over Christmas, when darker weather makes games more appealing. The end-of-year holidays are a key sales season for game and toy companies. Board games have gained popularity among 16- to 25-year-olds, who are now putting them "at the heart" of their social life, Koegler said. An international barometer compiled by Asmodee and Kantar in 2026 showed that 74 per cent of the so-called "Gen Z" thought that in-person experiences were more important than digital ones. Koegler also pointed to rising attendance at trade events such as Spiel Essen and Gen Con, and hobby stores engaging local player communities, as two indicators that Asmodee's efforts to engage players through in-person events were working. "We see increasing of sales (in hobby stores), which means an increase in sell-out from them, because they are this nexus of local communities," Koegler said. ORGANIZED PLAY SUPPORTS TRADING CARD GAMES Organized play also holds a strong place in the success of trading card games, a category that Koegler has previously described as extremely strong and lasting. "All the events are packed because people really engage," he said. The Netherlands' largest board game event Spellenspektakel, which also hosts Europe's biggest trading card game event CardCon, reported 33,000 visitors at its 2026 edition on November 7-8, with a sold-out first day. Asmodee's sales grew 18.4 per cent in the board game category and 51.6 per cent in trading card games during its most recent quarter that ended in September. Hasbro's earnings were also boosted by its flagship trading card game Magic: The Gathering ahead of the holiday season.

data.title: From Bollywood to Clippy: Nvidia scandal, Outlook glitch fuel meme storm
data.description: Nov 13 : Jensen Huang as a Bollywood matinee idol, as a character from "The Matrix" or donning a red velvet suit on a poster for an alternate-universe version of "The Spy Who Shagged Me": the Nvidia co-founder's extramarital affairs, including with a Chinese businesswoman, set the Internet afire this week. The storm of AI generated video and images, many of the clips were likely made with the help of Nvidia graphics chips, provided some light relief to a scandal that toppled one of the tech industry's most prominent CEOs, wiping out hundreds of billions of investor value and triggering investigations worldwide. The Huang memes competed for the spotlight with a raft of comedic takes on the more than 12-hour outage of Microsoft services including Outlook and Teams, topping off a week that kicked off with the latest Stephen Miller vampire memes after U.S. President Donald Trump named him as chief of staff, effective Monday. But it was humor on the crisis surrounding Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia that dominated many social media feeds, with many of the clips likely made using Nvidia graphics chips, RaviKunvariyaX quipped on X.  "Jensen is literally funding the infrastructure, selling the hardware, and collecting revenue while the internet uses his own technology to troll him," the user said. One widely shared image showed Jensen Huang in an Nvidia shirt turning away from logos for AI models including OpenAI, Google's Gemini and DeepSeek, then pointing at a woman labeled "Chinese Model," a play on the allegations surrounding his resignation.  A satire on X placed Jensen Huang and Alice Huang's faces over those of actors in the opening credits of the classic sit-com "Three's Company," about a man with two female roommates. Others included an AI-generated video with millions of views featuring US President Donald Trump, along others depicting what ostensibly happened behind the scenes at the chip giant. Nvidia was among the trending topics in popular platforms such as Reddit and X for most of this week. A more than 12-hour outage of Microsoft services, including Outlook and Teams, that sent some business scrambling for fax machines, phones and paper added fresh fodder for the meme factories late in the week. 'HAPPY FRIDAY' "No rush. Take your time ... Happy Friday," read one widely shared post, signed "Every corporate employee," X user omgsidewalks posted. The X post was viewed over 4 million times. Other memes imagined a role for Microsoft's much maligned 'Clippy' 90s-era virtual helper either causing or explaining the outage. Microsoft's services have been a repeat meme subject, including after a global IT outage in 2024 triggered by a faulty CrowdStrike update, that crashed Windows machines. "every year, microsoft should turn off outlook for an afternoon so we can all go outside and play with out friends :)," read another X post with thousands of views.

data.title: Nvidia's Huang turns to Paul Weiss, law firm that inked deal with Trump
data.description: WASHINGTON, Nov 13 : Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang turned to law firm Paul Weiss amid his rapid fall this week, tapping a firm that reached a controversial deal with President Donald Trump last year and whose own longtime leader was forced to step down in February. Huang resigned on Thursday after more than 30 years leading the top AI chipmaker, following reports that he had extramarital affairs with three women, including an Nvidia executive and Chinese businesswoman whom US intelligence suspects of being ​a Chinese spy. Paul Weiss, Nvidia and a spokesperson for Huang had no immediate comment on Friday about the nature of the law firm's work for Huang. New-York based Paul Weiss, with more than 1,500 lawyers, long has been a go-to for corporate boards and executives facing regulatory scrutiny, misconduct allegations or other reputational crises. It built a reputation pairing lucrative work for Citigroup and other business clients with liberal advocacy and fundraising for Democratic candidates, including Kamala Harris. But the firm drew sharp criticism within the legal profession and from Democrats last year after striking a deal with Trump to rescind an executive order the Republican president issued against it in March 2025. Trump's order suspended security clearances for the firm's lawyers and restricted their access to government buildings and officials, citing its internal diversity policies and its association with a prosecutor who investigated the president. Paul Weiss pledged in its settlement to dedicate $40 million in pro bono legal services to support "mutually agreed" projects with the White House, sparking similar deals by eight other law firms. Its longtime chairman Brad Karp defended the accord, calling Trump's order an existential threat.  The tumult facing Karp ramped up early this year, after emails surfaced showing Karp's extensive personal and business communications with the late convicted sex offender and financier Jeffrey Epstein. Karp resigned from his leadership post in February, saying the reports about Epstein had created a distraction that was not in the firm's interests. He has not been accused of wrongdoing. GO-TO FIRM FOR CORPORATE CRISES Paul Weiss has a stable of former senior Justice Department officials and others who frequently step in for clients when crisis strikes. BlackRock in 2021 hired partner Loretta Lynch, who was US Attorney General under President Barack Obama, to assist with an internal probe of former employees' claims of sexual harassment and discrimination. Huang is working with Paul Weiss partners Melinda Haag and Walter Brown, the New York Times reported on Thursday. Haag served as US attorney in San Francisco during the Obama administration. She and Brown did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not independently confirm which lawyers at the firm are representing Huang. The Republican leaders of several US House committees, including Foreign Affairs, addressed a letter to Brown on Thursday stating they wish to interview Huang in closed-door session next month. Haag successfully defended former Fitbit executive Katherine Mogal, who was acquitted in 2020 of federal charges alleging theft of trade secrets from a rival wearable-device maker. Brown is on the team defending Meta Platforms in a lawsuit by an Australian mining magnate over scam ads on Facebook showing him promoting fake cryptocurrency. Nvidia’s board has hired another top firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Kratz to conduct an independent investigation. That probe will be led by Wachtell’s Joon Kim, a former senior federal prosecutor in Manhattan.

data.title: Nvidia approached Arm CEO Haas to succeed Huang, FT reports
data.description: Nov 13 : Nvidia's board has approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis and sending shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll. Haas is among several candidates being considered to succeed Huang and there is no guarantee he will be offered the job or accept it, FT reported. The British chipmaker declined to comment, while Nvidia did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Reuters could not independently verify the report. Arm's US-listed shared pared losses after the report and were down more than 5 per cent. Nvidia's shares were down over 3 per cent.

data.title: German watchdog warns some cooling systems remain vulnerable to hacking
data.description: BERLIN, Nov 13 : Germany's information security office BSI warned on Friday of ongoing vulnerabilities in some of Danish firm Danfoss' industrial cooling appliances, following cyberattacks on refrigeration systems across Europe. The systems in question should be taken offline when possible or otherwise any connection should be secured via VPN, or Virtual Private Network, BSI said in a security advisory on its website. Hacking attacks on European supermarkets spread across the continent last week, hitting fridges and ​freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month. At least some of the refrigerator units affected used temperature control technology from Danfoss that was also targeted in the French ​attack.  The German office said IT security managers should also check whether they can install updates available from the company. It warned, however, that Danfoss had not yet provided sufficient software updates to counter the attacks. "Even new patches do not guarantee that further vulnerabilities in an affected product will not come to light in the near future. Industrial control systems should therefore not be directly accessible from the internet."   The United States last week also warned of a "cyber threat" to industrial refrigeration systems.

data.title: Neoclouds, AI stocks slide again as Nvidia turmoil rattles sector
data.description: Nov 13 : Shares of AI-related US companies dropped again on Friday, with neoclouds among the worst hit, fueled by fresh jitters over AI financing following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt exit. The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 declined 2.2 per cent, on pace to erase almost $870 billion in market value if the losses hold through the close. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index also shed 6 per cent, facing a more than $670 billion wipeout for the day. CoreWeave and Nebius Group, neocloud firms backed by Nvidia, slumped 10.8 per cent and 12.1 per cent, respectively, extending their sharp declines from Thursday when longtime CEO Huang stepped down after revelations of extramarital affairs. Nvidia, under Huang, has financed infrastructure built around its chips, a strategy that has driven demand but also raised questions about circular funding flows between the chipmaker and its customers. "It's a short-term death blow to the industry because the amount of vendor financing and financing guarantees that Nvidia and Jensen Huang stepped into are now over," said Thomas Hayes, chairman of Great Hill Capital LLC. Further, Nscale, a British cloud provider also backed by Nvidia, amended its IPO filing to say it expects to report a net loss of $1.7 billion in the nine months ended September 30, wider than the $433.3 million net loss a year ago. Chip stocks, widely regarded as among the biggest winners of the AI boom, also dropped. Advanced Micro Devices fell 10.2 per cent and Broadcom lost 6.7 per cent after both gained for the last five sessions. Memory chipmaker Micron Technology shed 5.6 per cent while data storage companies Western Digital and Sandisk dipped 7.7 per cent and 9.3 per cent, respectively. Photonic product makers Lumentum and Coherent, along with AI server makers Dell and HPE, fell between 6.2 per cent and 10.7 per cent each. Utilities and equipment suppliers exposed to the AI boom, including GE Vernova, Constellation Energy and Vistra, eased about 2 per cent to 3.3 per cent each. AI hyperscalers were also mostly lower, barring Meta Platforms, which rose 1.3 per cent. Oracle, Alphabet, Amazon.com and Microsoft fell between 0.1 per cent and 3.6 per cent. Nvidia's quarterly earnings and AI lab Anthropic's much-awaited public markets debut are set for next week and could prove to be catalysts for sentiment towards AI. "You have no idea what to expect from Nvidia. That's the problem. This company is pure uncertainty right now," said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers.

data.title: Dollar set for biggest weekly gain in two months
data.description: NEW YORK/GDANSK, Nov 13 : The dollar was on track for its strongest weekly rise in two months on Friday, holding near a 19-month high as rising bets on a larger Federal Reserve rate hike lifted US Treasury yields, while the yen hovered around 160 per dollar and kept traders alert for possible intervention from Tokyo. Hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials and this week's stronger-than-expected US inflation data have left traders weighing the prospect of a larger-than-usual Fed rate hike next month. Two-year Treasury yields have risen around 32 basis points so far this week to around 4.84 per cent, on course for their biggest weekly jump since April 2025. The euro was down 0.23 per cent at $1.103, after hitting its lowest level against the dollar since April 2025. It was on course for its fourth straight week of losses. The dollar was up 0.28 per cent to 0.837 against the Swiss franc and was set to snap two straight weeks of losses.  "The dollar is still firm and that's driven by a robust jobs report and an acceleration of the CPI," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex. "We've had a series of hawkish comments from Fed officials this week including from (New York Fed President John) Williams and (Fed Governor Christopher) Waller." Traders are pricing in a roughly 92 per cent chance of a 25-basis-point hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed.  The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, was up 0.1 per cent at 103.34, clinging to its highest since April 2025 and on track for its biggest weekly gain since September. That would be its third straight week of gains. YEN FOCUS           The yen was steady at 159.84 per dollar, around its weakest since early September, fuelling concerns about possible intervention. The currency has weakened about 1 per cent this week, on track for its biggest weekly loss since September.  Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday the government would respond appropriately to currency volatility. The Australian dollar was down 0.46 per cent at $0.678. The Aussie is the worst-performing G10 currency against the dollar so far this month. Australia is the only G10 country for which markets are pricing a rate cut next year. [AUD/]  The New Zealand kiwi weakened 0.29 per cent versus the greenback to $0.553 and was on course for its third straight week of losses. In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 4.73 per cent to $68,126.21. Ethereum declined 5.02 per cent to $1,914.61.

data.title: Fed's Warsh to take stock of AI revolution as US public grows wary
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 13 : Federal Reserve officials expect artificial intelligence will reshape the US economy, an idea that proponents of the technology in Silicon Valley have plastered on billboards and TV and pushed in public debate as they channel trillions of dollars into data centers and billions into their bank accounts. But how the region's new tech boom evolves, and on what timetable, remains a wild card for central bankers responsible for managing inflation and employment in the short term. In a public forum on Monday in San Francisco, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh will try to understand better the risks and benefits he and his colleagues may have to balance — from the possible large-scale loss of jobs to the promise of rapid economic growth and falling prices. The forum, the only scheduled public event of the five task forces Warsh established early in his tenure this year to review issues of major importance to the Fed, will take him to the epicenter of an emerging industry he sees as a "hinge point in history," even as last week's midterm elections sparked a backlash against rapid data center construction and raised the specter of deepening inequality. For all of AI's disinflationary potential, Warsh is convening the discussion while the frenetic AI buildout is having the opposite effect — driving up prices in a way that increasingly concerns many Fed officials, with no clarity for when it may let up and with the possibility the central bank may need to slow the very thing Warsh sees as revolutionary. More broadly, what seemed a clear proposition of supercharged growth and buoyant productivity when Warsh spoke while auditioning for the Fed job — he was also an investor in AI firms but sold his holdings under Fed ethics rules — is now at the center of a national debate that could change the industry's trajectory. Though driven by local politics, the concerns range from local land use to the impact on children's and societal mental health, the potential for stress in financial markets as capital is channeled through increasingly complex AI funding vehicles, and, most recently, risks to national security after revelations about a top tech industry executive's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. "We have to make sure that AI is used responsibly and ethically," Oakland Mayor Barbara Lee said recently as she joined a movement to ban local data center construction that has taken root just across San Francisco Bay. "It can't become a tool that compounds the biases that are already built into our systems. It can't be a tool for harm, for discrimination, or for displacement." EVOLVING VIEWS It may be difficult for participants in the three-hour forum on Monday to cover the sweeping set of issues that will determine whether AI deployment accelerates or slows, and therefore how deep an impact it might have on inflation, employment and other data the Fed watches. An agenda published by the San Francisco Fed says the event, including three panels of speakers bookended by comments from Warsh, will offer "input from a wide range of stakeholders on technology's implications for the economy and the labor market." It will be a homecoming of sorts for the Fed chief. He attended nearby Stanford University with some of the tech industry's leading figures and appointed one of them, Marc Andreessen, to chair the task force that will focus on AI, which Warsh has come to call "super intelligence" in line with President Donald Trump's wishes. Other members of the productivity and jobs task force include Chad Jones, a Stanford University economics professor now working with the internal think tank of AI firm Anthropic, which is on the verge of an initial public offering that would value the company at more than $1 trillion, and Asha Sharma, who runs Microsoft's Xbox business. Fed officials began focusing on AI even before Warsh took the helm, with the pace of research and discussion accelerating after the release of the ChatGPT generative AI chatbot in 2022 and the start of breathtaking changes for a technology that a decade ago had trouble telling a cat from a kitchen table. Thanks to breakthroughs in large language models and the massive assemblage of computing power, AI is now solving advanced math and medical problems, turning novice entrepreneurs into software engineers, and offering bespoke "agentic" services that can do legal or scientific research or take over personal bill-paying and daily planning. While Warsh initially saw AI as providing a downdraft on inflation through higher productivity — a free ride of sorts that could allow central bankers to keep interest rates lower than would otherwise be expected — he has taken a more nuanced view since arriving at the Fed in May. The shift reflects the uncertain timetable for productivity benefits, the potentially inflationary investment needed to realize them, and views about job-market impacts that range from a lift-all-boats boost to a Dickensian world of chronic underemployment. 'TRULY HISTORIC' INVESTMENT At a forum in Oakland in September, where the city's mayor issued her warning about AI, Fed Governor Lisa Cook, whose academic research focused on innovation, reiterated concerns that AI would lead to "at least a temporary increase in the unemployment rate" and possibly a jump in the underlying level of joblessness. Fed Governor Michael Barr raised similar concerns on Thursday, saying the US should prepare for "serious short-term disruptions" to the job market depending on how fast AI is deployed and whether it remains broadly available and affordable to businesses regardless of size. For the moment, though, AI investments are propping up US growth, stock-market gains, and consumer and business spending that might otherwise be unremarkable. "You have this investment that is truly historic. You are talking railroad-plus-interstate-highways-historic," Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said recently at a chamber of commerce event in South Carolina where attendees pumped him for insight on what the AI boom might mean. "If that historic investment does not pay off and people scale back, you worry what is going to happen." Although all the members of the task force Warsh picked are from the tech world, neither they nor the Fed chief will have the last word on how any recommendations find their way into Fed policy. That matter will be left to officials like Barkin, who said he hoped the discussion on Monday would cover the full landscape of issues. "I'm hopeful we'll hear the strongest possible evangelist's view, as well as the strongest possible other view," Barkin said. "Then we'll have a chance to wrestle with it."
